caption: The drawing features two powder horns rendered in naturalistic detail. Both objects are depicted in shades of brown, showing variations in color and texture that represent the natural material of the horns, with the top horn displaying a slightly darker and more even brown hue while the bottom horn shows lighter and darker variations. The upper horn is positioned with its wider end to the left and its narrow, capped end to the right; the narrow end has a metal or wooden spout attached. There is a line of inscribed or engraved text along the length of the upper horn. The lower horn is shown diagonally below, with its wider open end facing forward and the narrowed tip pointing up and left. The tip appears to have a translucent or light-colored material, possibly glass or bone, secured by a ring. There are visible engravings or inscriptions on the lower horn as well, though they appear less distinct than those on the top horn. Both horns are centered on a plain, light beige background. The artist’s name, "STANLEY MAZUR," is written in small, clear letters toward the lower left of the composition.
title: Powder Horn
